name: Avatar group
purpose: A set of people shown as one object: overlapping Avatar discs, primary-first, with an overflow counter when the set is longer than the display cap. The unit of meaning is the GROUP ('five people are on this approval'), not the individuals.
$differsFromAvatar: Avatar (GATED) is the single disc — initials, image or icon, sizes small/medium/large, optionally linking to one profile. Avatar group adds NOTHING to that disc: the disc markup, its surface, its ring and its round exemption are copied verbatim. What it adds is the ARRANGEMENT — negative-margin overlap, a separator ring, a display cap, an overflow counter, and a single accessible name for the whole set. Rule of thumb: one person = Avatar; a countable set of people = Avatar group; a list of people you act on individually = List-items.

props.name: size
props.$note: 32 / 44 / 64 — Avatar's own ramp, copied exactly. Overlap follows at -8 / -12 / -16 (a quarter of the disc), so a member always shows enough of itself to read as a separate person.

props.name: max
props.$note: Display cap. Members beyond it collapse into the overflow counter. 3 is a specimen choice, not a ruled default.

props.name: interactive
props.$note: ⛔ 'members' is offered at MEDIUM and LARGE ONLY — a 32px interactive disc breaches the ruled 44px min-hit-area. Small sets that must be clickable take 'group': one 44px target for the whole stack.

props.name: announce
props.$note: ⚠ TWO ACCESSIBLE SHAPES FOR ONE COMPONENT — a decision, not a feature. See $openQuestions.

variants.name: group-announced
variants.use: the default — one accessible name for the set, discs hidden from AT; the set is the meaning

variants.name: roster
variants.use: a real list where every member is announced; use when the individuals ARE the content

variants.name: members-interactive
variants.use: each disc is its own 44px target linking to that person (medium and large only)

variants.name: group-target
variants.use: the whole stack is one 44px button — the correct answer for small stacks

tokens.surface: tertiary/background/hover — the disc fill, from Avatar
tokens.stackRing: background/default — the 2px separator between overlapping discs. ⚠ see $finding-ring
tokens.radius: 50% — EXEMPTION: Avatar is one of the two documented exemptions to the angular brand rule (the other is Badge)

$finding-ring: ⚠ THE ONE REAL WEAKNESS, SHOWN IN THE SPECIMEN RATHER THAN DESCRIBED. The separator ring binds background/default, so the stack only separates correctly ON THE PAGE. Dropped onto a card (tertiary/background/default) or a hover wash, the ring is the wrong colour. In LIGHT mode the card is also white and the defect hides; in DARK mode the page is #1A1A1A and the card is #1F1F1F, so the rings read as dark halos around each disc. The specimen carries an on-card block so Dave can see it in both themes side by side. The honest fixes are a surface-keyed token or a --stack-ring the consumer sets; both are Dave's, and neither is invented here (grey-tint and ink swaps are surface-never-swap items).

accessibility.theCoreDecision: A stack of discs read out one-by-one is noise ('J L, P A, S O, plus three'). So in the DEFAULT form the GROUP carries the accessible name and the count in words — role="img" with an aria-label naming every visible member AND the overflow ('Approvers: Jordan Lee, Priya Anand, Sam Okafor, and 3 more') — and the individual discs are aria-hidden. This is the PROPOSED reading, not a ruled one.
accessibility.theAlternative: The 'roster' variant does the opposite: a real <ul> where each member is announced, the count comes from the list itself, and there is no overflow disc because a roster does not cap. It is for the case where the individuals genuinely are the content.
accessibility.colourIsNeverAlone: The overflow counter's '+3' is never the only carrier of the count — the group's accessible name spells it as 'and 3 more'.
accessibility.targetSize: Interactive members are built at MEDIUM (44) and LARGE (64) only. The 32px interactive disc is not built at all, because the ruled 44px min-hit-area forbids it and no gate reads that token; enforcement here is by hand, by omission. Small stacks that must be clickable become one 44px group target.

antiPatterns: ⛔ Never make a 32px disc interactive — it breaches the ruled 44px min-hit-area, and no gate will catch it for you.
Never announce every disc in the default stacked form; a stack read disc-by-disc is noise, which is the whole reason the group carries the name.
Never let '+3' be the only place the count exists — spell it in the accessible name.
Never use Avatar group where the user must act on individuals one at a time; that is List-items.

Never use the class name 'avatar' for the disc here — canon/type.css binds .avatar to a 14px composite which silently beats the per-size composite on the large disc. The class is avg-face for exactly this reason.
REVIEW Never drop the group onto a card without deciding the separator ring first — the ring binds the page colour and will be wrong (see $finding-ring).

tokenValidation.result: PASS — snippet gate rc=0, 0 failures on this file. Every declared var matches the store in BOTH modes. No new token minted; one is PROPOSED (a surface-keyed stack ring) and is Dave's, see $finding-ring.
tokenValidation.rebind: ⚠ FINDING, per the gated-component runbook step 2. The gated Avatar's ring var carries a DEPRECATED pair — its light leg exists only in tokens/_manifests/depricate-tokens.json — AND Avatar does not declare that var in its manifest, so _validate_snippets.py has never seen it. This file declares the var and binds it to the live border/subtle (#E1E1E1 light / #808080 dark). Avatar itself was NOT edited: it is a gated shared artefact and the fix is the conductor's to merge.
tokenValidation.typeDivergence: Avatar's large disc uses a raw 24px font-size, which is off the component ramp and part of the type-composite debt. This file uses .t-cm-section-label (20px, weight 500), the nearest ramp rung — a PROPOSED divergence from the parent, declared rather than silent. Small and medium use .t-cm-ctl-12 and .t-cm-ctl-14, which preserve Avatar's weight 500 on-ramp. TYPE-002 contribution: 0.

provenance.$note: Itinerary row 57 (2026-07-14), 'Avatar group — Stacked avatars', P2 Depth. Verified absent first-hand #203 (ls + content grep across avatar/group/stack/cluster/facepile). Built #203 Wave 3b Lane K from the gated Avatar, untouched. No Figma node binds this component.

responsive.behaviour: inline-flex; the stack does not reflow — it caps. When width is short the answer is a lower max, not a wrap.

dimensions.$note: Sizes are Avatar's ramp verbatim. Overlap is a quarter of the disc at every size.

$openQuestions: TWO ACCESSIBLE SHAPES FOR ONE COMPONENT is a decision, not a feature. Should Avatar group ship both the group-announced and roster forms, or should one be the component and the other be a documented composition of plain Avatars?
The separator ring's token — see $finding-ring. A surface-keyed token, a consumer-set var, or accept the page-only limitation?
Display cap default of 3 is a specimen choice.
Should the overflow counter be interactive by default (it opens the full set), or passive?
Stacking order: this specimen puts the FIRST member on top, so the set reads left-to-right like a hand of cards. Last-on-top is equally common.
